solve: Fitted by T-3689, by eye, to the left half of Melander & Henderson's stereograph 'No. 51. Residence of Mahlon D. Ogden, Esq.' (Views of Chicago Ruins, Great Fire of October 1871; LOC LC-USZ62-57071, cph 3b04902), cropped from the Library's scan to 620 x 650 px. The house stands behind the elms of its grounds, its front and veranda to the camera, the rubble of a burnt brick house and an iron fence in the foreground. The stand was set in Washington Square about 55 m south of the house's front, for a stereo lens of about 930 px, so that the eaves (y about 140 px), the veranda's roof and the ground line fall where the print shows them; then the heading was moved until the front's two corners did: heading 9.6 degrees, the horizon at y 258 px. UNCERTAINTY: large; the house is half hidden by trees in a small print. It is good for the storeys, the five-bay front, the veranda and the low roof, not for a dimension. LIGHT: overcast.
